_about: Tables for body/MUSCULAR.md. Rendered by build-body-data.py. Muscle groups are the functional model (anatomy real; the selection and the stats proposed). Activation profiles are illustrative percentages of maximal voluntary contraction (%MVC), read from EMG studies where one exists and the keeper's estimate where none does; every profile is a Composer-scale data task to refine (combat keeper's note, item 5). mark: rex | proposed | open.

fatigue_rates.title: Three-compartment fatigue model (3CC): rates by joint
fatigue_rates.source: Xia and Frey Law 2008 (J Biomech): muscle in resting, active, fatigued compartments; F = fatigue rate active to fatigued, R = recovery rate fatigued to resting, per second. Fitted values from Frey Law, Looft and Heitsman 2012: ankle F 0.00589 R 0.0182; shoulder F 0.00058 R 0.00168; a 2018 extension adds a rest multiplier. MUS-3CC

endurance_time.title: How long a hold lasts at a given effort (Rohmert-type endurance curve)
endurance_time.source: Rohmert 1960 and later fits: endurance time falls steeply with %MVC; below about 15% MVC a hold is sustainable for a long time (the ergonomic design limit). Numbers here are the keeper's reading of general curves, not one study. MUS-ROH

activations.source: Shape from EMG literature where it exists (inverted row and suspension rows: lats, mid trapezius, biceps, rear deltoid at 50 to 60% MVIC; climbing postures: middle and lower trapezius 35 to 60%; MUS-EMG). Hauling rope is ChatGPT's illustrative profile (COMBAT.md 4b). Every other profile is the keeper's estimate and a data task to refine. The columns are the groups by id; a blank is 0.

training.title: Training, adaptation and disuse constants
training.source: Protein 1.6 g/kg/day is the plateau for resistance-training gains (Morton et al. 2018 meta-analysis, BJSM; MUS-PROT). DOMS peaks 24 to 72 h and clears by 7 days (MUS-DOMS). Muscle protein synthesis stays raised 24 to 48 h after lifting (textbook). Supercompensation (gain after recovery) is the Banister logic applied per group. Detraining: strength holds for about 2 to 3 weeks then falls; muscle mass loss is faster than strength loss (textbook, medium). Novice gains are fast (10 to 30% strength in 8 to 12 weeks), trained gains slow.

injuries.title: Muscle and tendon injuries
injuries.source: Strain grading I to III is clinical standard; recovery times are typical ranges (textbook). Risk factors: fatigue, cold, no warm-up, a load far above the group's development, prior injury.

limb_strength.title: How a limb's Strength is computed from its groups (proposed answer to the replace-or-compute question)
limb_strength.source: Rex left open whether muscle replaces per-limb Strength or Strength is computed from it (COMBAT.md 4b; ChatGPT: replaces). This table is the 'computed' reading, offered because it keeps STATS.md's Strength number alive for every system that already reads it while the muscles underneath make it per limb and trainable by what you do. Weights are the keeper's.
columns: Formula (development x (1 - fatigue) x condition, per group)
rows: weighted mean of the right arm's groups, scaled to the STATS 1 to 20 range
